page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top. Two text columns; the right column is set beside a narrow column of marginal references (2. Cor., Nempe quia...). Below the columns, full-width continuation lines and a short catchword-like line "strum." at the right. Footnote marks b and c in the left column are keyed to notes printed below in the body.

main_text.p: catorum, atque illius etiam prauitatis, cum qua mihi per omnem vitam pugnandum eft b, memoriam omnem de pofuiffe, & me iuftitia Chrifti gratis donare, ne unquam in iudicium veniam c.
Nouit peccatum, pro nobis peccatum effet, vt nos efficeremur iuftitia Dei in eo.
b Ierem. 31. v. 34. Quia propitiabor iniquitati eorum, & peccati eorum non recordabor amplius.

Pfalm. 103. v. 3. 4. Qui remittit omnes iniquitates tuas, qui sanat omnes infirmitates tuas. Qui redimit de fouea vitam tuam, qui coronat te in misericordia & miserationibus. Et v. 10. Non secundum peccata nostra fecit nobis, neque secundum iniquitates nostras retribuit nobis. Et v. 12. Quantum distat Oriens ab Occidente, distare fecit à nobis praeuaricationes nostras.
Rom. 7. v. 24. 25. Miser ego homo: quis me eripiet ex isto corpore mortis? Gratias ago Deo per Iesum Christum Dominum nostrum.

page.notes: <note side="right">2. Cor. 5. v. 19. Nempe quia Deus erat in Christo, mundum reconcilians sibi, non imputando eis peccata ipsorum, pofuitque in nobis sermone hunc reconciliationis.</note> <note side="right">Et v. 21. Fecit enim, ut qui non nouit peccatum...</note> The printed page has marginal and footnote letters b and c, and the page contains a few faint or damaged words at the edges which are uncertain. Marked readings with [?] are doubtful; the number of the Psalm verse is partly cut.
